head: SkyVoxel: 3D weather radar app shows storms you can spin and slice
dek: SkyVoxel, a new $2.99 iPhone and iPad app, turns US Doppler radar from NOAA's NEXRAD network into a 3D model of a storm that you can rotate, tilt and cut through. It was #14 in Weather on the US App Store's paid chart on 16 November.
details: It has three views: a full 3D volume, solid shells at the radar levels you pick, and a cross-section from the ground to the top of the scan along a line you draw. You pick any NEXRAD site for its latest scan, and the app explains radar terms. It's a one-time purchase with no subscription. The maker says it's a tool for enthusiasts and not a replacement for official warnings.
where: iPhone and iPad, $2.99 one-time on the App Store, US radar sites (out since 15 November)
means: If you follow storms in the US, you can see how tall a storm is and where its strongest parts sit instead of a flat radar map.
todo: Use it alongside official alerts: in severe weather, follow the National Weather Service and local authorities, as the maker advises.
